title: Compare a PLS and a CB analysis
skills: Estimands of PLS, PLSc and CB-SEM

brief.text: Open the service-quality example (SYNTHETIC data): service quality (SQ) → satisfaction (SAT) → loyalty (LOY), with a direct path SQ → LOY. All constructs are reflective, and the measurement model has been validated. Run CB-SEM (ML, the example's setting) and then classic PLS-SEM on the same model.

tasks.prompt: Enter R² of LOY from CB-SEM (ML).
tasks.feedbackWrong: Not the expected value. Run CB-SEM with ML and read R² of LOY.

tasks.prompt: Enter R² of LOY from classic PLS-SEM.
tasks.feedbackWrong: Not the expected value. Switch the method to classic PLS-SEM (not PLSc) and read R² of LOY.

tasks.prompt: Why is R² of LOY lower with classic PLS?

options.text: PLS explains composites that contain measurement error, which attenuates their correlations; CB-SEM explains error-free common factors.
options.feedback: Correct. Different estimands, not a better or worse fit.
R² of composites and of factors are different quantities; neither is a fit index here.
If the common-factor model holds, CB-SEM estimates the factor R² consistently.

tasks.prompt: What would you expect from PLSc on this model?

options.text: Values close to CB-SEM, because PLSc also targets common factors.
Values close to classic PLS, because it is a PLS method.
options.feedback: The consistency correction changes the estimand to the common factor.
Disattenuation raises correlations among reflective constructs.

tasks.prompt: How should both results appear in a paper?

options.text: Report the method chosen for the research question as the main analysis; if the other is shown, label it with its estimand and explain the difference.
options.feedback: Correct. Never merge or average them.
Averaging estimates of different quantities produces a number that estimates nothing.

options.text: Report whichever gives the higher R².
options.feedback: Choosing the method by its result is outcome-driven reporting.

hints: Both methods report R² for LOY, but of different things. Of what?
Recall how measurement error affects correlations between composites.
PLSc and CB-SEM share an estimand; classic PLS has another.

solution.text: CB-SEM (ML): R²(LOY) ≈ .520 and standardised SAT → LOY ≈ .598. Classic PLS: R²(LOY) ≈ .421 and SAT → LOY ≈ .534. PLSc: R²(LOY) ≈ .523 and SAT → LOY ≈ .602, close to CB-SEM.

The difference is the estimand: composites with their measurement error versus common factors. Report the analysis suited to your construct theory, label any comparison with its estimand, and never merge or average results.
